extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutions preparing NIH/NIAID grant applications (PIs, trainees, small businesses, sponsored research offices)
extracted.subtask_description: An index of NIAID sample grant applications, summary statements, and accompanying forms/resources intended to illustrate expectations for many NIH grant mechanisms and related application materials. Useful for applicants preparing R, K, F, U, SBIR/STTR, and institutional proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific FOA (Funding Opportunity Announcement) instructions as authoritative for page limits, required forms, and submission format rather than relying solely on sample applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use samples as examples, not definitive current rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Although these applications demonstrate good grantsmanship, time has passed since these grant recipients applied; the samples may not reflect the latest format or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult current NIH/NIAID instructions and FOAs; NIAID posts new samples periodically. Treat sample strategy/structure as illustrative rather than prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and reuse conditions for sample materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of these applications is copyrighted; awardees provided express permission for NIAID to post them for educational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use material (data, writing, graphics) for nonprofit educational purposes only if the material remains unchanged and the principal investigators, awardee organizations, and NIH NIAID are credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA/confidentiality considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH responds to FOIA requests for grant applications and summary statements, the material will be subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH must protect confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / Section 508 conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample applications have been reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure application materials meet Section 508 and institutional accessibility standards when preparing documents (e.g., readable by screen readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: R01 purpose and expected project duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The R01 is the NIH standard independent research project grant, intended to provide 4 or 5 years of support to complete a project, publish, and reapply before the grant ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select R01 when you need sustained support to complete a defined research program; review sample R01 applications and summary statements for structure and approach examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 eligibility and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 small grants support new research projects that can be carried out in a short period with limited resources; awarded for up to 2 years and are not renewable. R03s are not intended for new investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use R03 for short, focused projects with limited scope; ensure proposed work fits the limited timeframe and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (Research Enhancement Award) purpose and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: R15 supports small-scale research projects to expose students to research and strengthen the research environment at institutions that have not been major recipients of NIH support; awards up to 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions with limited NIH history should emphasize student training, institutional capacity building, and feasible small-scale research plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 purpose and intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 funds novel scientific ideas, model systems, tools, agents, targets, and technologies that have potential to substantially advance biomedical research. R21s are not intended for new investigators and are not evidence of a path to an independent research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use R21 for exploratory, high-risk/high-reward projects with limited preliminary data; articulate novelty and potential impact clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21/R33 phased award structure and milestone-based transition
rubrics_metrics.description: R21/R33 supports a two-phased award without a break in funding: an initial R21 phase for milestone-driven exploratory/feasibility studies with a possible transition to an R33 phase for expanded development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition to R33 depends on achievement of negotiated milestones; define clear, measurable milestones and success criteria in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR (R41/R42/R43/R44) small business program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR (R43/R44) and STTR (R41/R42) support domestic small businesses to engage in R&D with potential for commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate commercial potential, a viable small business partner, and appropriate intellectual property/commercialization plans; consult NIAID Small Business Programs resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: K01 Research Scientist Development Award eligibility and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: K01 supports those with a research or health-professional doctoral degree and research development plans in any areas of the NIAID scientific mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a clear career development plan and mentoring plan aligned with NIAID mission; include measurable training and productivity goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist award requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: K08 supports those engaged in biomedical or behavioral research who hold a clinical doctoral degree (e.g., M.D., D.V.M., O.D.) and a professional license to practice in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on mentored, translational research plan and documentation of clinical credentials and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: K23 Mentored Patient-Oriented Research award requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: K23 supports those with a clinical doctoral degree who commit to patient-oriented research and have potential to develop into productive clinical investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize patient-oriented research aims, mentorship, and a career development plan targeted to clinical investigation skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: F31 NRSA predoctoral fellowship purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: F31 provides research experience to predoctoral scientists (NRSA individual fellowship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate training aims, mentoring, research plan appropriate to predoctoral level, and career goals in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: G11 (EARDA) institutional capacity-building purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: G11 provides funds to eligible institutions to establish or enhance an office of sponsored research and other research infrastructure needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe institutional needs for research administration capacity building and how funds will be used to strengthen sponsored research operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: U01 cooperative agreement purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: U01 supports a discrete, specified, circumscribed project for investigators to perform in their areas of specific interest and competency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the specific project scope clearly and describe the investigators' specific expertise and roles; cooperative agreements imply substantial programmatic involvement by NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigor and reproducibility resources and examples are provided (Scientific Rigor Examples, Authentication Plan Examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must address scientific rigor, including experimental design, biological variables, authentication of key resources, and reproducibility strategies; use provided examples for structure and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan requirement and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Data Management and Sharing Plans and examples are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a DMSP that describes data types, standards, preservation, access, and timelines; follow NIH DMSP policies and use examples as templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model organism sharing plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Model Organism Sharing Plans (Complex, for Mice, Simple) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include a plan for sharing model organisms (availability, distribution, repositories) consistent with NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting protection of human subjects training
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Letter to Document Training in the Protection of Human Subjects is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentation that key personnel have completed required human subjects protection training; use sample letters to meet documentation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-Time (JIT) information submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample NIAID Request for Just-in-Time Information is provided to illustrate JIT materials and process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand which documents may be requested at JIT (e.g., IRB approvals, Other Support) and prepare templates to expedite submission when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Organization System (FOS) review preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources on Preparing for a Foreign Organization System (FOS) Review are listed for international grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign organizations should prepare required documentation and understand institutional eligibility and review elements specific to FOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward documentation and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Subaward Templates and Tools (from the Federal Demonstration Partnership) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use approved templates for subawards and ensure budgets, scopes, and compliance information are clearly documented and consistent with prime application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NIH required forms and format pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotated SF 424 Grant Application Forms, SF424, Format Pages, Biosketch Format Pages, Other Support Format Page, Reference Letters, Additional Senior/Key Person Profile Format, Additional Performance Site Format are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required forms exactly as specified (SF424 family, biosketch, other support, performance sites, reference letters); use annotated examples to ensure proper content and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Leadership Plan for Multiple PI applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of Project Leadership Plans for Multiple PI Grant Applications are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing Multiple PIs, submit a leadership plan delineating roles, decision-making, resource sharing, and communication among leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person months and effort reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Example calculations in the 'Usage of Person Months' Q&A are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effort in person months consistently across budget and key personnel sections; use examples to calculate and present effort correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable appendix materials guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of Allowable Appendix Materials are provided to clarify what may be included in appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH rules for allowable appendix content; do not include disallowed materials to avoid administrative rejection or reviewer disregard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Project Outcomes in RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Project Outcomes Description for RPPR (Research Performance Progress Report) is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples to prepare clear, concise RPPR descriptions of accomplishments, outputs, and changes in aims or personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal research assurance and VAS requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OLAW's Sample Documents for animal research assurances and reports, Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section (VAS), and Sample Animal Study Proposal are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare VAS sections with required detail on animal use, welfare, justification, and procedures; use OLAW samples and the VAS worksheet to ensure compliance.
